newsitem.title: CHINA: China to issue 20 bln yuan listed bonds.
newsitem.headline: China to issue 20 bln yuan listed bonds.

text.p: China will begin issuing this month 20 billion yuan ($2.4 billion) of discounted bonds that will be listed on domestic stock exchanges, the official Xinhua news agency said on Friday.
The news agency said the bonds would be offered between January 22 and February 17 and would be listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges.
Xinhua said the two-year debt would be offered to domestic institutions through public auction and then listed on the two exchanges.
The Futures Herald has estimated that China would issue 240 billion yuan worth of domestic debt this year while securities sources have said the total could be as high as 250 billion.
That would compare with 195.2 billion yuan in 1996.
China has been issuing more domestic debt both to raise needed funds and to strengthen its domestic financial market.
In the past China had forced the public to buy bonds at below-market interest rates but it is now attracting investors with market-based interest rates.

It also shifting to the public tender system for its debt offers, relying on domestic financial institutions to create a primary market and then listing some of the bonds to make them attractive trading vehicles for small investors.
